variants.when: Models with a service reminder (wrench symbol) in the multi-information display, such as the 2019 Outlander and Mirage
steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have been changed or the scheduled service was done.
Leave the ignition OFF. The reminder cannot be cleared with the ignition ON.
Tap the multi-information display switch on the instrument cluster until the service reminder screen with the wrench symbol appears.
Press and hold the switch (about 1 to 2 seconds, depending on the model) until the wrench symbol flashes.
While it is flashing, tap the switch once. The dashes change to CLEAR and the time and distance to the next service appear.
variants.note: If nothing is pressed for about 10 seconds the screen backs out. When service is due the display shows dashes instead of the time and distance left.

variants.when: North American models with a pressure sensor in each wheel, such as the 2008–2013 Outlander and 2011–2013 and 2017 Outlander Sport
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker, and check the spare if it is monitored.
Drive normally. There is no reset button: the light goes out by itself after a few minutes of driving once the pressures are right.
If it stays on after about 10 minutes of driving, recheck the pressures and look for a slow leak or puncture.
variants.note: If the light blinks for about a minute and then stays on, the system has a fault or a wheel without a working sensor is fitted; a reset will not clear it. New sensors must be registered by a shop with a scan tool.

notes: Mitsubishi's service reminder is cleared with the single switch on the instrument cluster, with the ignition off. North American Mitsubishis checked here have no driver TPMS reset: the light clears itself after driving once the pressures are corrected.
